method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Always request a ketone check in an unwell child with diabetes** — ketones can be raised even with normal glucose.
claims.source_text: Always request a ketone check in unwell children with established diabetes (ketone levels may be raised even in normoglycaemia)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Never advise omission of basal/background insulin**, even when unwell, fasting or hypoglycaemic.
claims.source_text: Never advise omission of basal or background insulin in children with diabetes, even when unwell, fasting or hypoglycaemic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat nausea/vomiting as insulin deficiency until proven otherwise.** Ketones over 3, especially with vomiting, mean high DKA risk and likely admission.
claims.source_text: Consider nausea/vomiting as a sign of insulin deficiency in a child with established diabetes until proven otherwise … Children with diabetes and ketones >3, especially if vomiting, are at high risk of diabetic ketoacidosis and likely require hospitalisation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interpreting results (T1DM):** hypoglycaemia 3.9 mmol/L or below · normal pre-meal 4–7 · normal post-meal 4–10 with ketones under 0.6 · high over 11 with ketones 0.6 or more · very high over 15 (check ketones), with ketones over 1 needing insulin.
claims.source_text: BGL and ketone interpretation in type 1 diabetes BGL Ketones Hypoglycaemia ≤3.9 mmol/L Normal pre-meals 4-7 mmol/L <0.6 mmol/L Normal post-meals 4-10 mmol/L <0.6 mmol/L High >11 mmol/L ≥0.6 mmol/L Very High >15 mmol/L (check ketones) >1 mmol/L (insulin required)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Increase monitoring: finger-prick BGL at least 2–4-hourly including overnight (1–2-hourly if more unwell).** Confirm CGM readings by finger prick, especially under 4 or over 10 mmol/L.
claims.source_text: Confirm any continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) readings with finger prick BGL, especially if BGL <4 mmol/L or>10 mmol/L … At least 2-4 hourly finger prick BGL for children without CGM, including overnight BGL 1-2 hourly if more unwell
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluids: BGL under 14 — sugar-containing fluids** (diluted juice, electrolyte drinks); **BGL 14 or more — sugar-free fluids.**
claims.source_text: If BGL <14: encourage sugar-containing fluids eg diluted juice, electrolyte drinks If BGL ≥14: encourage sugar-free fluids
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not advise omitting insulin even with hypoglycaemia.** Hypoglycaemia with ketones over 0.6 mmol/L means insulin **and** carbohydrate deficiency and needs urgent medical attention.
claims.source_text: Do not advise to omit insulin, even in the setting of hypoglycaemia/illness … Hypoglycaemia with ketones >0.6 mmol/L suggest insulin and carbohydrate deficiency and warrants urgent medical attention
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pump users may need a temporary basal rate of 70% of normal** for hypoglycaemia while unwell (follow the child's plan first). Reduce the next insulin dose by 10% if BGL is under 4 more than once.
claims.source_text: For persisting hypoglycaemia whilst unwell, a temporary basal rate of 70% of normal may be required, with ketone monitoring … Reduce next dose insulin by 10% if BGL <4 on more than one occasion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hyperglycaemia with ketones under 0.6:** usual plan, with a correction at the next rapid-acting dose. **Ketones 0.6 or more = insulin deficiency:** give an additional insulin bolus.
claims.source_text: Hyperglycaemia with ketones <0.6 Treat as per the child's usual insulin treatment plan Most children should be advised to give an insulin correction with their next rapid-acting insulin dose eg mealtime Hyperglycaemia with ketones ≥0.6 Indicates insulin deficiency Treat with additional insulin bolus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sick-day bolus = extra rapid-acting insulin on top of usual doses, tabulated as 10% or 20% of the total daily dose (TDD).** TDD is all rapid plus long-acting insulin in a day; if unknown, **estimate 1 unit/kg** from recent weight.
claims.source_text: Total daily dose (TDD) Sick day dose (rapid-acting insulin in addition to usual doses) 10% 20% … This is all the insulin (rapid and long-acting) that a child has in a day. … If the child uses flexible dosing strategies or family are unaware/unsure of usual doses, estimate TDD using 1 unit/kg based on most recent weight
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypoglycaemia with ketones 0.6 or more needs hospital** for fluid and insulin.
claims.source_text: Hypoglycaemia with ketones ≥0.6 Suggests both carbohydrate and insulin deficiency Commence hypoglycaemia treatment as above Requires hospital presentation for fluid and insulin treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pumps deliver only rapid-acting insulin, so failure or disconnection carries a high DKA risk.** If BGL stays high or ketones are 0.6 or more: check the line, change catheter, tubing and reservoir; **BGL over 15 = treat as pump failure** and give supplemental insulin by subcutaneous injection.
claims.source_text: Children on pumps receive only rapid-acting insulin and are therefore at high risk of DKA if the pump fails or is disconnected If BGL persistently elevated or ketones ≥0.6 … Check for problems with the pump or delivery system … Change the catheter, tubing and insulin reservoir If BGL >15, treat as pump failure Give supplemental insulin as a subcutaneous injection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ketones may rise for 1–2 hours after a bolus** before falling if treated correctly.
claims.source_text: Following an insulin bolus, ketones may increase for 1-2 hours but are then expected to decrease if treated correctly
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Faulty pump:** disconnect; if BGL and ketones are normal, give **1/6 of TDD as rapid-acting insulin by injection every 4 hours** until diabetes-team review.
claims.source_text: 'I think my insulin pump is faulty' Disconnect pump Check BGL and ketones If within normal range, give 1/6 total daily dose by rapid-acting insulin injection every 4 hours until review by diabetes care team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe hypoglycaemia (confused, unconscious or seizing): IM glucagon — under 25 kg 0.5 mg (half vial, 0.5 mL); over 25 kg 1 mg (full vial, 1 mL).** Seizure: call 000.
claims.source_text: Intramuscular glucagon dosing for severe hypoglycaemia If child confused, unconscious or having a seizure Inject 1 mL of H2O into the vial containing glucagon 1 mg, gently agitate to dissolve Use a syringe to draw up the entire solution (1 mL) from the vial and administer dose depending on weight <25 kg: give 0.5 mg (half of vial, 0.5 mL) >25 kg: give 1 mg (full vial, 1 mL) … 'My child is having a seizure' Give glucagon IM Call '000' for an ambulance
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Minidose SC glucagon** for BGL under 4 mmol/L when oral treatment fails or is not tolerated **but there is no CNS impairment.** Reconstitute 1 mg in 1 mL; 1 insulin-syringe unit = 10 microg.
claims.source_text: Minidose glucagon is used to manage hypoglycaemia (BGL <4 mmol/L) in a child with diabetes, when usual oral treatments have been unsuccessful or cannot be tolerated, but the child does not have CNS impairment … Re-constitute the full 1 mg vial in 1 mL of sterile water and then use an insulin syringe to draw up to the 1 'unit' mark on the insulin syringe. 1 unit = 10 microg of reconstituted glucagon solution
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Minidose initial dose:** under 2 years 20 microg (2-unit mark) · 2–15 years 10 microg per year of age (1 unit per year) · over 15 years 150 microg (15-unit mark).
claims.source_text: Minidose glucagon - initial doses for subcutaneous administration Age (years) Dose of glucagon Mark on insulin syringe <2 20 microg (0.02 mg) 2 unit mark 2-15 10 microg per year of age 1 unit per year of age >15 150 microg (0.15 mg) 15 unit mark
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check BGL at 30 minutes.** 5.5 mmol/L or more: hourly BGL and cut the next insulin by 10%. Under 5.5: **second and then third minidose at double the initial dose**; still under 5.5 after the third, go to hospital. Discard reconstituted glucagon after 24 hours.
claims.source_text: Check BGL at 30 minutes If ≥5.5 mmol/L, check BGL hourly, reduce next insulin by 10% If <5.5 mmol/L, give 2nd minidose of glucagon at double initial dose … If <5.5 mmol/L, give 3rd minidose of glucagon at double initial dose If BGL remains <5.5 mmol/L after 3rd dose, advise to present to hospital After glucagon is reconstituted, keep in refrigerator and discard after 24 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Advise ED if:** BGL cannot be kept above 4 mmol/L · BGL under 5.5 despite 3 glucagon minidoses · ketones over 0.6 with vomiting or not tolerating oral · **ketones over 3 at any time** · cannot maintain hydration · confused, lethargic or severe abdominal pain · deteriorating or unclear condition.
claims.source_text: Inability to maintain BGL >4 mmol/L despite treatment as per hypoglycaemia flow chart BGL remains <5.5 mmol/L despite 3 minidoses of glucagon Ketones persist >0.6 mmol/L and child is vomiting/unable to tolerate oral intake Ketones >3 mmol/L at any time Inability to maintain hydration at home eg limited oral intake, ongoing losses Child is confused, lethargic, suffering severe abdominal pain The child deteriorates or their underlying condition is unclear
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent DKA review:** ketones over 3 (especially with vomiting or abdominal pain), rapid breathing, drowsiness, or ketones rising (especially over 1.5) despite extra boluses.
claims.source_text: Concerning signs that the child requires urgent medical review for DKA include: Ketones >3, especially with vomiting and/or abdominal pain Rapid breathing Drowsiness or altered conscious state Rising ketones (especially if >1.5) despite additional insulin boluses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Run out of insulin: never advise skipping a dose** — arrange a script. **Too much given:** extra carbohydrate and recheck BGL; **too little:** check BGL and ketones.
claims.source_text: 'I've run out of insulin' Never advise skipping a dose of insulin See GP for script … If too much, give extra serve of carbohydrates and recheck BGL If too little, check BGL and ketones, and monitor. Extra insulin may be required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Diabetes mellitus: management of unwell children with established diabetes at home' (Last updated July 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Diabetes_mellitus__management_of_unwell_children_with_established_diabetes_at_home/, retrieved 2026-09-23
